flows.summary: Turn a repo into a first flow map: list its entry points, brief independent mapping passes, check each pass, and vote them into one map.

steps.name: Maintainer lists every entry point the repo exposes into inventory.json
steps.notes: Adapter chosen by flowmap.toml [[entry]]; detect_entries only auto-detects rails/nextjs/fastapi, never cli. Other adapters (fastapi/rails/nextjs .entries) are reachable by config but not used in this repo.

steps.name: Maintainer writes one brief per independent pass (run id + bottom-up/top-down method)
steps.notes: Fills RUN_SPEC.md template with METHODS/STACK text. The passes themselves (agents writing runs/<id>.json) have no code in this repo.

steps.name: Maintainer checks each pass's anchors exist and every entry point is placed
steps.notes: Read-only; result is stdout + exit code. Also run by each mapping agent on its own output before finishing.

steps.name: Maintainer votes the passes into one map with evidence levels and a list of open questions

flows.summary: Name the proposed flows and settle split votes, then rebuild the map so human decisions become the fixed vocabulary and confirmed evidence.

steps.name: Maintainer re-runs reconcile after naming flows in flowmap.toml and pinning answers in decisions.json
steps.notes: decisions.json endpoint_flow pins flow placement ('confirmed'); confirmed_steps raises evidence; canonical_new_flows drops the new: prefix once the id is in the vocabulary. decisions.json and flowmap.toml are hand-edited, no command writes them.

steps.name: Maintainer regenerates briefs so later passes place steps under the named flows
steps.notes: Inferred from vocabulary_text switching between discovery mode and a fixed flow table.

flows.summary: See the map: flows, their steps and the code each step runs, as Mermaid diagrams and an interactive atlas page.

steps.name: Maintainer generates Mermaid diagrams at system, flow and step zoom
Maintainer builds the interactive atlas page and browses flows, steps and components
steps.notes: Reads map.json, inventory.json and QUESTIONS.md (split votes are scraped back out of the generated markdown).

flows.summary: Review a PR by where it lands on the map: which flows and steps it touches, what it can reach, and what code the map doesn't know.

steps.name: Reviewer places a base..head diff on the map (steps touched, call-graph reach, off-map code)
steps.notes: Prints markdown to stdout only; the pr-lens skill consumes it. Re-inventories both revisions via git show.

steps.name: Reviewer paints the change onto the atlas as a PR overlay
steps.notes: Triggered by --pr base..head=label; one overlay per flag.

flows.summary: Ask which entry points (and flows) can reach a given function before changing it.

steps.name: Developer asks which entry points and flows can reach a file:symbol
steps.notes: Without the 'impact' subcommand it only prints graph size. endpoint_flows reads map.json, so it fails before reconcile has run.

observations: Two implementations of 'place a diff on the map': flowmap/atlas.py:overlay re-derives changed/new symbols and call-graph reach itself using lens helpers, instead of sharing logic with flowmap/lens.py:main. They already differ: overlay skips test files and '<module>' hits, lens.main counts '<module>' as a changed symbol and classifies steps by anchor match first.
flowmap/atlas.py:build calls flowmap/diagrams.py:Diagrams.system and throws away the Mermaid it returns, only to get self.matrix set as a side effect.

flowmap/atlas.py:split_votes scrapes split votes back out of the human-facing QUESTIONS.md written by flowmap/reconcile.py:write_questions_md (regex on '→ placed'): a generated report doubles as a data interface, and the vote data is never written to map.json.

The call graph is rebuilt from scratch in four places: flowmap/callgraph.py:__main__, flowmap/diagrams.py:Diagrams.__init__, flowmap/lens.py:main and once per --pr in flowmap/atlas.py:overlay (plus Diagrams again in flowmap/atlas.py:build).

flowmap/adapters/cli.py:_files lists commands with git ls-files, so a new, untracked command script is invisible to inventory while every other tool reads the worktree; flowmap/config.py:detect_entries never auto-detects the cli adapter, so CLI repos depend on flowmap.toml.
flowmap/verify.py:anchor_ok checks each dotted part of 'Class.method' independently anywhere in the file, so a method cited under the wrong class still passes.
flowmap/reconcile.py:canonical_new_flows merges proposed flows transitively at Jaccard >= 0.3 via union-find, so a chain of partially overlapping proposals can collapse into one flow.

Docstrings and messages still name another repo's layout ('tools/flowmap/...', 'backend/app' in flowmap/callgraph.py and flowmap/reconcile.py:write_map_md), though the real path is flowmap/ under config.root().
